line: Wind lifts dust: a dust storm in the Sahara, and a dust devil on Mars.

photos.title: Dust Storm, Sahara Desert, Algeria/Niger Border, Africa
photos.alt: A wall of brown dust rolling across the Sahara, seen from orbit, with small clouds above its front.

photos.title: The Devil is in the Details
photos.alt: A pale dust devil on orange Martian plains, seen from above, with its long dark shadow.

line: Thick ice in layers: a Greenland glacier, and buried ice in a cliff on Mars (colours enhanced).

photos.title: Jakobshavn Calving Front
photos.alt: The broken white edge of Jakobshavn Glacier in Greenland, seen from a NASA aircraft.

photos.title: Underground Martian Ice Deposit Exposed at Scarp
photos.alt: A steep Martian slope seen from above, where a thick band of buried ice shows as bright blue.

line: Runny lava builds wide, gentle volcanoes: Hawaii, and Olympus Mons on Mars.

photos.title: iss068e068973
photos.alt: The island of Hawaii in a blue ocean, seen from the space station, with snow on its two big volcanoes.

photos.title: Olympus Mons
photos.alt: Olympus Mons on Mars seen from above: a huge round volcano with a crater at its top and a cliff around its base.

line: Lava flows on Mauna Loa in Hawaii, and a pit on the Moon that may open into a lava tube.

photos.title: Earth Observation
photos.alt: Dark lava flows spreading down the slopes of Mauna Loa from its summit crater, seen from the space station.

photos.title: Marius Hills Pit -- Lava Tube Skylight?
photos.alt: A small, dark, round hole in the grey cratered ground of the Moon's Marius Hills, seen from above.
